craniospinal_compliance.physiological_equivalent_description: Craniospinal compliance: the volume the craniospinal space accepts per mmHg of ICP rise. The bedside quantity behind PVI, RAP and 'compensatory reserve'. Falls as the cranium is loaded; a low value means a small further volume produces a large ICP rise. Computed as 1/(E*(ICP_baseline - Pcv)) from the fitted elastance coefficient E.
craniospinal_compliance.bound_source: craniospinal compliance 0.5-1.1 mL/mmHg in adults; <0.4 is reduced reserve
craniospinal_compliance.caveat: No healthy controls exist in this dataset - all four recordings are ICU patients. Healthy bounds are from literature, not from a control group measured with this pipeline.

csf_outflow_resistance.physiological_equivalent_description: Resistance to CSF absorption (Rout) - the quantity a lumbar infusion study measures directly. Elevated in normal-pressure hydrocephalus and IIH; abnormally LOW suggests a CSF leak, an open shunt, or a mis-specified cranial/spinal absorption split. Computed as the parallel combination of the cranial (0.069) and spinal (0.931) routes.
csf_outflow_resistance.caveat: No healthy controls exist in this dataset - all four recordings are ICU patients. Healthy bounds are from literature, not from a control group measured with this pipeline.

arterial_compliance.physiological_equivalent_description: Cerebral arterial compliance: the arterial bed's volume response within a cardiac cycle. Sets how much of each beat's stroke volume the arteries themselves absorb, and is the parameter cerebrovascular reactivity indices (PRx) are sensitive to.
arterial_compliance.bound_source: anchored on M3's literature default Ca = 0.03 mL/mmHg; no human range
arterial_compliance.caveat: No healthy controls exist in this dataset - all four recordings are ICU patients. Healthy bounds are from literature, not from a control group measured with this pipeline.

collateral_outflow_resistance.physiological_equivalent_description: Resistance of the vertebral venous plexus, the collateral route cerebral blood takes when the jugular is obstructed. A high value means outflow CANNOT redistribute and the jugular is functionally the only exit - which is what makes a compression raise ICP.
collateral_outflow_resistance.bound_source: anchored on M3's default Rvvs = 0.04 mmHg.s/mL; NO published human range
collateral_outflow_resistance.caveat: No healthy controls exist in this dataset - all four recordings are ICU patients. Healthy bounds are from literature, not from a control group measured with this pipeline.

jugular_resting_area.physiological_equivalent_description: Resting internal jugular cross-section implied by the fitted tube-law stiffness. STREAMED AS QUALITY CONTROL, NOT AS A DIAGNOSIS: Model_6/structural_diagnosis shows the fit drives this to 5-12 cm2 (about 205 mL of jugular) which is roughly ten times physiological, and that this artefact is what causes the model's ICP pulse-amplitude failure. A bedside ultrasound falsifies it in thirty seconds. Read a value outside the healthy band as evidence the FIT is wrong, not that the patient is.
jugular_resting_area.bound_source: supine IJV cross-section ~0.8-2.0 cm2; posture- and respiration-dependent
jugular_resting_area.caveat: No healthy controls exist in this dataset - all four recordings are ICU patients. Healthy bounds are from literature, not from a control group measured with this pipeline.

sagittal_sinus_pressure.physiological_equivalent_description: Superior sagittal sinus pressure, the downstream boundary for cerebral venous outflow. Elevated in venous sinus stenosis and IIH. STREAMED AS A NEGATIVE CONTROL: it is the one parameter that stayed inside its healthy band in all four recordings, so a pipeline that reports it as pathological has a bug rather than a finding.
sagittal_sinus_pressure.caveat: No healthy controls exist in this dataset - all four recordings are ICU patients. Healthy bounds are from literature, not from a control group measured with this pipeline.
